in perso  CORAM:
 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE AMIT SHARMA  ORDER % 19.01.2023

The present petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C filed on behalf of the petitioners, seeks quashing of FIR No. 0503/2020, under Sections 498A/406/354/509/506/34 IPC, registered at P.S.
Paschim Vihar, East, Delhi and all other consequential proceedings emanating therefrom including the chargesheet pending before the court of Ms. Aneeza Bishnoi, learned Metropolitan Magistrate,
Mahila Court-05, West District, Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi.

entities.text: Mahila Court-05, West District, Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The marriage between petitioner no.1/husband and respondent no.2/wife was solemnized on 31.08.2017 as per Hindu rites and ceremonies.
No child was born out of the said wedlock.
Due to matrimonial differences between petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2, the parties started residing separately from 23.07.2020.

Subsequently, respondent no.2/complainant lodged an FIR against petitioner no.1 (husband),
petitioner no. 2 (mother-in-law), petitioner no. 3 (since deceased father-in-law), petitioner no.4 (brother-in-law), petitioner no.5 (brother-in-law) & petitioner no.6 (cousin brother-in-law).

sentences.text: On 08.11.2021, parties arrived at a settlement/agreement before Learned Principal Judge, Family Courts, Tis Hazari District Courts, and as per the said settlement/agreement, petitioner no.1 has agreed to pay an amount of Rs. 45 lakhs to the respondent no.2/wife towards full and final settlement of all her claims including istridhan, permanent alimony and maintenance - present, past and future.

entities.text: Principal Judge, Family Courts, Tis Hazari District Courts
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The copy of the aforesaid settlement/agreement dated 08.11.2021 is on record (Annexure-B).

In terms of the said settlement, the marriage between the parties stands dissolved by a decree of divorce dated 27.11.2021, passed by Mr. Raj Kumar Tripathi, Judge Family Court (West District) Tis Hazari, Delhi, (Annexure-C).

entities.text: Judge Family Court (West District) Tis Hazari, Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Further, as per the settlement/agreement, an amount of Rs. 30 Lakhs has already been paid to respondent no.2 and the remaining amount of Rs. 15 Lakhs has been paid to her in court today, by means of a demand draft.

Petitioner no. 1, 4 to 6 and complainant/respondent no. 2 are present before the Court, and have been duly identified by their respective counsel, as well as the Investigating Officer, SI Sweta , P.S.
Paschim Vihar, East, Delhi.
Petitioner no. 2 appears through video conferencing and has been duly identified by their respective counsel, as well as the Investigating officer SI Sweta, P.S. Paschim Vihar, East, Delhi.
A demand draft bearing no. 041561 dated 06.12.2022 for Rs. 15 Lakh drawn on Bank of Baroda has been handed over complainant/Respondent No.2, who acknowledges the receipt of the same.
The complainant/respondent No.2 states that the matter has been settled with the petitioners and she has no objection if the FIR is quashed.
She further states that all the terms of the agreement have been complied with.
In view of the settlement between the parties, learned APP for the State also has no objection if the present FIR is quashed.

In Gian Singh v. State of Punjab, (2012) 10 SCC 303, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has recognized the need of amicable resolution of disputes by observing as under:-
"61. ...

entities.text: Gian Singh v. State of Punjab, (2012) 10 SCC 303
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In other words, the High Court must consider whether it would be unfair or contrary to the interest of justice to continue with the criminal proceedings or continuation of criminal proceedings would tantamount to abuse of process of law despite settlement and compromise between the victim and the wrongdoer and whether to secure the ends of justice, it is appropriate that criminal case is put to an end and if the answer to the above question(s) is in the affirmative, the High Court shall be well within its jurisdiction to quash the criminal proceeding."

In view of the aforesaid circumstances, and the fact that the parties have put a quietus to the dispute, no useful purpose will be served in continuing with the present FIR No. 0503/2020, under Sections 498A/406/354/509/506/34 IPC, registered at P.S.
